newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs stay depressed despite good activity.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs stay depressed despite good activity.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCCs) showed no sign of waking up from their torpor on Wednesday even though there was no shortage of vessels being fixed, brokers said.

"Unfortunately there seem to be too many Japanese re-lets kicking around. I presume that's what's making people a bit nervy," one broker said. "I hope it has now bottomed out. There is certainly volume around."
Brokers put VLCCs from the Middle East to most destinations at around W47.5. This represented a 2.5 point fall from Tuesday for vessels to Japan.
Rates to Singapore and westwards were little changed, although some older ships fetched only W45.

West Africa/U.S. Gulf and North Sea/USAC VLCCs, meanwhile, were steady at W67.5, with 130,000 tonne vessels also unchanged at W92.5/95. Brokers said the fixture of the Sea Star from Mongstad to St Croix at W84 for Hess was not representative of the market as its destination was especially close to the loading area.
Inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonne remained at about W92.5, down almost 10 points from last week, as a lack of cargoes continued to depress the market.
The 80,000 tonne Mediterranean market dipped to W105 from W107.5, with reports that the Messapia was being fixed as low as W100 from Sidi Kreir to Falconara for API.
"It's the usual story, too many vessels and not enough cargoes," an Italian broker said, also citing the planned closure of berth two at Novorossiisk for 22-23 days next month.
Berth two is the second largest crude berth at Novorossiisk and can take ships of 60,000-90,000 dwt.
Fuel oil rates were little changed at W185 for 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont and W195 in the Med.
Caribs/upcoast rates were also steady, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W220 and 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil at W165. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
